data.name: Khaleeq
data.gender_notes: Khaleeq is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root kh-l-q, meaning 'to create'. In Islamic context, Khaleeq refers to Allah (God) as the Creator of the universe. The name Khaleeq carries the meaning “Creator, Maker” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khaleeq usually hope their child will grow to embody creator, maker and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khaleeq total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

It is a reminder of Allah's power and omniscience in creating the universe and all living beings. The name is also used to express respect, reverence and devotion towards Allah.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Khaleeq is deeply spiritual as it emphasizes the belief in the supremacy of Allah as the Creator. It is a call to remember and appreciate Allah's infinite wisdom, power and mercy in designing and creating the universe and all living beings. The name serves as a reminder of our connection to Allah and the importance of living in accordance with His will and guidance. Ultimately, the name Khaleeq invites us to reflect on the majesty and wonder of Allah's creation and the role we play as His creatures in this grand design.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 4, Page 389 The name Khaleeq carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Khaleeq ibn Al-Khawlan, who was one of the first converts to Islam in the city of Taif, was a prominent leader among the Muslims there. He fought bravely in the Battle of Hunayn against the Meccans and was martyred during the Battle of Taif.

historical_references.reference: The Biographical Dictionary of the Prophet Muhammad's Companions and Successors, by Ibn Hajar Al-Haytami, Volume 2, Page 141
historical_references.context: Khaleeq ibn Al-Khawlan was a prominent and well-respected figure in Taif before embracing Islam. He was a poet, a leader, and a respected member of the community. After his conversion to Islam, he dedicated himself to spreading the faith and defending the Muslim community from their enemies.
